::: {.remark}

#### Use in statistics and machine learning

Let $\noise$ be the noise in a new outcome $\Outvar$,
and let $\Rvar$ be the difference between the true mean $\mean = \E{\Outvar}$ and a prediction $\eoutvar$:

$$\Rvar \eqdef \mean - \eoutvar$$

The mean of $\Rvar$ is minus the bias of the prediction:

$$
\ba
\E{\Rvar}
&= \E{\mean - \eoutvar}
&& \text{(definition of } \Rvar \text{)} \\
&= \mean - \E{\eoutvar}
&& \text{(expectation of a difference; } \mean \text{ is a constant)} \\
&= -\paren{\E{\eoutvar} - \mean}
&& \text{(factor out } -1 \text{)} \\
&= -\bias{\eoutvar}
&& \text{(definition of bias)}
\ea
$$

The variance of $\Rvar$ is the variance of the prediction:

$$
\ba
\Var{\Rvar}
&= \Var{\mean - \eoutvar}
&& \text{(definition of } \Rvar \text{)} \\
&= \Var{\eoutvar}
&& \text{(a constant shifts a variable without changing its variance, and a sign flip does not change it either)}
\ea
$$

Substituting these two results into the theorem,
with $\sqf{-\bias{\eoutvar}} = \sqf{\bias{\eoutvar}}$,
gives the squared prediction error of the new outcome as

$$
\E{\sqf{\noise + \Rvar}} = \varpar + \Var{\eoutvar} + \sqf{\bias{\eoutvar}},
$$

where $\varpar$ is the [residual variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-irreducible-error).
The statistics notes define the bias of a prediction and the training data it depends on,
and state this result for predictions as the
[bias, variance and noise decomposition](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#thm-epe-decomposition),
with its exercise, worked example and definition of the residual variance.

:::
